newsitem.title: PERU: Rescuers evacuate hundreds stranded in Peru snow.
newsitem.headline: Rescuers evacuate hundreds stranded in Peru snow.

text.p: Rescue workers used helicopters and road-clearers on Tuesday to evacuate hundreds of people stranded in their vehicles on a highway in Peru's Andes by a snowstorm that has already led to six deaths.

Soldiers and civil defence workers battled through a wall of snow to gain access by road to people stuck in vehicles since Friday when a vicious snowstorm blitzed the highway 11,650 feet (3,500 metres) above sea level, authorities said.

Rescue teams cleared parts of the 50-mile (80 km) highway, allowing some people to drive their vehicles -- including crowded passenger buses -- to safety at nearby Abancay, 380 miles (610 km) southeast of Lima, Civil Defence official Luis Barra told Reuters.
As snow stopped falling for the first time since Friday, the army airlifted others off the road by helicopter and planned flights throughout Tuesday.
About half of the 1,000 people originally stranded were still stuck on the mountain by midday on Tuesday but most of them were had received aid from rescue workers.
Soldiers, who walked to the snowbound area on Sunday, found the bodies of six people, including three infants, who froze to death inside their trapped vehicles.
Weather changes, caused by the El Nino current warming surface waters in the Pacific Ocean, have resulted in unusually cold temperatures this year in the Andes mountain range.
